contentBlocks.text: Last week you explored properties of matter. This week: a new topic, how living things interact in ecosystems!

A food chain shows how energy moves through an ecosystem. Producers (like grass) make their own energy from sunlight. Consumers (like a rabbit, then a fox) eat other living things for energy. Decomposers (like fungi and bacteria) break down dead organisms, returning nutrients to the soil. Build a simple food chain: grass → rabbit → fox. Which role does each organism play — producer, consumer, or decomposer?
You just built a real food chain, tracing energy through an ecosystem! Tomorrow we'll connect multiple food chains into a food web.

objectives: Define producer, consumer, and decomposer roles in a food chain
Correctly identify each role in the grass → rabbit → fox food chain
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Review last week's matter-properties work briefly.
2. Introduce producer/consumer/decomposer roles.
3. Have the child identify each role in the grass/rabbit/fox chain.
4. Complete the worksheet.
5. Preview tomorrow's food-web lesson.
differentiationTips: Struggling: use arrows to show energy flow direction (grass → rabbit → fox) as a visual anchor
Ready for more: ask the child to build their own 3-organism food chain using animals/plants they know
This opens the course's ecosystems thread from its own description, using a simple, well-established food-chain model
teacherGuide.answerKey: Grass = producer. Rabbit = consumer (eats the producer). Fox = consumer (eats the rabbit). Decomposers (like fungi) aren't in this chain but would break down any of these organisms after death.
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: Directly addresses NGSS Grade 5 Life Science standard 5-LS2-1: developing a model to describe matter cycling among plants, animals, decomposers, and the environment, opening this week's ecosystems thread.
